investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-14T13:48 with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment cannot provision a new agent because the org-level agent limit is exhausted, blocking the entire remote-agents feature check suite.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call. The eval's observability account or org has reached the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents (100), preventing any new agent from being created. Because all downstream checks (state, runtime) depend on a successful agent creation, they cascade-fail with the same 409 error. This is a quota exhaustion condition, not a service outage.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} on check remote-agent-create (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:06.622Z, latencyMs 1250)
Sibling check remote-agent-state returned the identical 409 body (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:07.616Z, latencyMs 994)
Sibling check remote-agent-runtime returned the identical 409 body (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:08.530Z, latencyMs 914)
All three checks share featureId remote-agents and all evidence objects are empty, confirming no agent was ever provisioned and no vmId or remoteState was captured
The error message explicitly states the hard limit: 'limit is 100', indicating a quota ceiling rather than a transient infrastructure fault

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (30000ms), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota enforcement layer, not due to a timeout or infrastructure degradation
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The observability eval org/account has accumulated 100 live swarm agents — likely from prior eval runs that created agents but did not successfully clean them up (e.g., teardown steps failed or were skipped), causing agents to persist and exhaust the quota.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform a pre-run cleanup or quota check before attempting agent creation, so stale agents from previous runs accumulate over time until the limit is hit.
[Possible] A recent increase in eval run frequency or parallelism caused more agents to be created per unit time than are being deleted, gradually filling the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a platform configuration change, causing a previously-sufficient headroom to become exhausted.
[Less likely] A separate workload or user in the same org is consuming agent quota concurrently with the eval account, reducing available slots.

reproductionSteps.details: Verify the response returns 100 agents. If it does, quota is confirmed exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the eval service account, sorted by creation time. Look for agents that are not in an active/in-use state and were created by previous eval runs.

reproductionSteps.details: After deletion, re-run POST /api/agents to confirm a 201 is now returned and quota is no longer exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return passing status with vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready].

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Checks Failing with 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No agent can be provisioned, so downstream state polling and runtime readiness checks cannot proceed and produce no required evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally per the eval environment). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T13:48:06–08Z), that cap was already at or above the limit, causing every POST /api/agents call to return 409 with code "conflict" and inner message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three checks, all checks fail at the same point with identical error payloads, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever collected.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' combined with the inner 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' indicates the swarm layer rejected creation because the quota ceiling (100) has been reached, not because of a transient network or auth failure.

All three checks failed within a 2-second window (13:48:06–13:48:08Z) with low latency (914–1250 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure fault.
The evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream state or runtime data was collected.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of which can be populated without a successful agent creation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 live agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota and blocking all new agent creation.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown after each run, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit.
[Possible] A separate workload or automated process in the same org/environment created agents concurrently, consuming quota before the eval run could proceed.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is misreporting the current agent count as at-limit when it is not.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether the org is at or near the 100-agent limit.

reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents with a valid agent creation payload
reproductionSteps.details: Expect HTTP 409 with code 'conflict' and inner message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is exhausted.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (HTTP 409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T13:48Z with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no runtime response or chat readiness can be validated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is rejecting all POST /api/agents requests with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness attempts to create a fresh agent at the start of each run; because the quota ceiling is already met, agent creation fails before any lifecycle, state, or runtime checks can execute. This is a resource-limit exhaustion on the swarm layer, not a service crash or network outage. There is no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals in the supplied data, so impact is scoped to the eval environment's ability to provision test agents.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (endedAt 13:48:06.622Z), remote-agent-state (endedAt 13:48:07.616Z), and remote-agent-runtime (endedAt 13:48:08.530Z).

All three 409 responses carry the identical nested error payload: {"code":"conflict","message":"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"}, confirming a single shared quota gate is blocking all checks.

Latencies for all three failing calls are well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (914 ms, 994 ms, 1250 ms vs. 20000 ms warning / 60000 ms outage), meaning the swarm rejected requests immediately rather than timing out — consistent with a quota guard returning fast.
The check config marks remote-agent-runtime as required: false, limiting the blast radius to eval coverage rather than a hard service gate.

No evidence of passing sibling checks or alternative endpoints exists in the supplied data, ruling out a partial-route failure and pointing to a quota condition that affects the entire agent-creation path.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval or test agents from previous runs were not cleaned up, causing accumulated agent objects to exhaust the 100-agent quota ceiling over time.
[Likely] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/delete step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.

[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval environment and other workloads (e.g., staging, developer sandboxes), and concurrent usage from those workloads has consumed the remaining capacity.
[Less likely] The quota ceiling itself was recently lowered by a configuration change on the swarm backend, causing a previously sufficient limit to become insufficient.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents and reporting quota exceeded even when slots are available.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after stream open because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. The required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated, confirming the stream was terminated at session negotiation, not during generation.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response during session open indicates either: (a) the harness process is not running or not deployed at the expected address, or (b) the harness is running an incompatible version whose route for session open no longer exists at the expected path. The stream never advanced past `generation_start`, so no image frames or artifact URLs were produced. This failure is scoped to the eval environment's harness configuration and does not, by itself, confirm a production user-traffic outage — however, the environment field is marked "production", which warrants urgent verification.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. No `generation_completed` frame was emitted.
Required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both absent from the collected evidence, matching the check message: 'Missing expected evidence: frameTypes, imageUrlPresent'.
Latency was only 2018 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a timeout.
The check is marked `required: true` and the environment is `production`, making this a blocking signal.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The harness process is not running or has crashed at the host/port referenced by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL, causing all session-open requests to receive a 404.
(Likely) A recent harness deployment changed the session-open route path or API version, making the existing URL stale and returning 404 for the old path.

(Possible) The LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or path prefix) in the production eval runner, pointing to a non-existent or wrong service instance.
(Less likely) A network policy, load balancer rule, or service mesh configuration change is intercepting the request and returning a synthetic 404 before it reaches the harness.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately verify that the harness process is running and healthy at the host and port specified by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL in the production eval runner environment.
Curl or HTTP-probe the session-open endpoint directly from the eval runner host to confirm whether a 404 is returned and inspect the response body for routing clues.
If the harness was recently redeployed, compare the current harness API version's route manifest against the URL path the eval runner is calling to detect a path mismatch.
If the harness is down, restart or redeploy it and re-run the image-generation-stream check to confirm recovery.
If the URL variables are stale or wrong, update LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL to the correct endpoint and re-run the eval.

Because the environment is marked 'production', determine whether real image-generation requests are also failing by checking production request logs or error-rate metrics for SESSION_OPEN_FAILED — do not assume eval failure equals user-facing outage without that signal.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight harness reachability eval that performs a lightweight HTTP health-check (e.g., GET /health or /ping) against LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL before any stream eval runs, so harness-down failures are caught and reported separately from stream logic failures.

Add an eval that asserts the `frameTypes` array contains at least one intermediate progress frame (e.g., `generation_progress`) in addition to `generation_completed`, to catch cases where the stream completes but skips expected intermediate states.
Add an eval that validates the artifact URL returned in the completion payload is a non-empty, well-formed URL, catching cases where `imageUrlPresent` is true but the URL is malformed or empty.
Add a version-compatibility eval that checks the harness-reported API version against the expected version contract, catching incompatible deployments before stream evals run.

Add a latency-bracket eval that fails if stream completion occurs in under a configurable minimum threshold (e.g., 500 ms), which would flag suspiciously fast 'completions' that are actually early error exits.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after stream open because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. The required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated, confirming the stream was terminated at session negotiation, not during generation.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response during session open indicates either: (a) the harness process is not running or not deployed at the expected address, or (b) the harness is running an incompatible version whose route for session open no longer exists at the expected path. The stream never advanced past `generation_start`, so no image frames or artifact URLs were produced. This failure is scoped to the eval environment's harness configuration and does not, by itself, confirm a production user-traffic outage — however, the environment field is marked "production", which warrants urgent verification.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. No `generation_completed` frame was emitted.
Required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are both absent from the collected evidence, matching the check message: 'Missing expected evidence: frameTypes, imageUrlPresent'.
Latency was only 2018 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a timeout.
The check is marked `required: true` and the environment is `production`, making this a blocking signal.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The harness process is not running or has crashed at the host/port referenced by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL, causing all session-open requests to receive a 404.
(Likely) A recent harness deployment changed the session-open route path or API version, making the existing URL stale and returning 404 for the old path.

(Possible) The LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured (wrong host, port, or path prefix) in the production eval runner, pointing to a non-existent or wrong service instance.
(Less likely) A network policy, load balancer rule, or service mesh configuration change is intercepting the request and returning a synthetic 404 before it reaches the harness.

reproductionSteps.label: Confirm the configured harness URL is set and reachable
reproductionSteps.command: echo $LOCAL_HARNESS_URL && echo $SWARM_BASE_URL

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the harness session-open endpoint directly to reproduce the 404
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v "${LOCAL_HARNESS_URL}/" 2>&1 | head -40

reproductionSteps.label: Check whether the harness process is running on the expected host
reproductionSteps.command: ps aux | grep harness

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect recent harness deployment logs or container status for crash or restart events
reproductionSteps.details: Check the deployment orchestrator (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, systemd) for the harness service status and recent exit codes.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the failing eval in isolation after confirming harness is up
reproductionSteps.details: Trigger the image-generation-stream check manually and observe whether SESSION_OPEN_FAILED recurs or the stream now emits generation_completed and an artifact URL.

affectedAreas.label: Agent Runtime Harness
affectedAreas.reason: The 404 is returned by the harness at session open. The harness is either not deployed, crashed, or running an incompatible version at the configured URL.

affectedAreas.label: Image Generation Stream Routing
affectedAreas.reason: The media-generation feature's stream routing depends on a successful session open with the agent runtime. A harness 404 prevents any progress or completion frames from being emitted.

affectedAreas.label: LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL Configuration
affectedAreas.reason: The error message explicitly names these environment variables as the configuration surface to verify. A misconfigured or stale value would cause every session-open attempt to target a non-existent endpoint.

affectedAreas.label: image-generation-stream Eval Check (production)
affectedAreas.reason: This required check is marked production and is currently in a fail state, blocking the health signal for the entire media-generation feature.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately verify that the harness process is running and healthy at the host and port specified by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL in the production eval runner environment.
Curl or HTTP-probe the session-open endpoint directly from the eval runner host to confirm whether a 404 is returned and inspect the response body for routing clues.
If the harness was recently redeployed, compare the current harness API version's route manifest against the URL path the eval runner is calling to detect a path mismatch.
If the harness is down, restart or redeploy it and re-run the image-generation-stream check to confirm recovery.
If the URL variables are stale or wrong, update LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL to the correct endpoint and re-run the eval.

Because the environment is marked 'production', determine whether real image-generation requests are also failing by checking production request logs or error-rate metrics for SESSION_OPEN_FAILED — do not assume eval failure equals user-facing outage without that signal.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight harness reachability eval that performs a lightweight HTTP health-check (e.g., GET /health or /ping) against LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL before any stream eval runs, so harness-down failures are caught and reported separately from stream logic failures.

Add an eval that asserts the `frameTypes` array contains at least one intermediate progress frame (e.g., `generation_progress`) in addition to `generation_completed`, to catch cases where the stream completes but skips expected intermediate states.
Add an eval that validates the artifact URL returned in the completion payload is a non-empty, well-formed URL, catching cases where `imageUrlPresent` is true but the URL is malformed or empty.
Add a version-compatibility eval that checks the harness-reported API version against the expected version contract, catching incompatible deployments before stream evals run.

Add a latency-bracket eval that fails if stream completion occurs in under a configurable minimum threshold (e.g., 500 ms), which would flag suspiciously fast 'completions' that are actually early error exits.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) on POST /api/agents
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-14T13:48 with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment cannot provision a new agent because the org-level agent limit is exhausted, blocking the entire remote-agents feature check suite.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call. The eval's observability account or org has reached the maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents (100), preventing any new agent from being created. Because all downstream checks (state, runtime) depend on a successful agent creation, they cascade-fail with the same 409 error. This is a quota exhaustion condition, not a service outage.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} on check remote-agent-create (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:06.622Z, latencyMs 1250)
Sibling check remote-agent-state returned the identical 409 body (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:07.616Z, latencyMs 994)
Sibling check remote-agent-runtime returned the identical 409 body (endedAt 2026-06-14T13:48:08.530Z, latencyMs 914)
All three checks share featureId remote-agents and all evidence objects are empty, confirming no agent was ever provisioned and no vmId or remoteState was captured
The error message explicitly states the hard limit: 'limit is 100', indicating a quota ceiling rather than a transient infrastructure fault

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (30000ms), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota enforcement layer, not due to a timeout or infrastructure degradation
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The observability eval org/account has accumulated 100 live swarm agents — likely from prior eval runs that created agents but did not successfully clean them up (e.g., teardown steps failed or were skipped), causing agents to persist and exhaust the quota.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform a pre-run cleanup or quota check before attempting agent creation, so stale agents from previous runs accumulate over time until the limit is hit.
[Possible] A recent increase in eval run frequency or parallelism caused more agents to be created per unit time than are being deleted, gradually filling the quota.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a platform configuration change, causing a previously-sufficient headroom to become exhausted.
[Less likely] A separate workload or user in the same org is consuming agent quota concurrently with the eval account, reducing available slots.

reproductionSteps.label: List all active swarm agents for the eval org to confirm quota saturation
reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (authenticated as the eval service account)
reproductionSteps.details: Verify the response returns 100 agents. If it does, quota is confirmed exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to create a new agent to reproduce the 409
reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents with a valid agent creation payload (authenticated as the eval service account)
reproductionSteps.details: Expect HTTP 409 with code 'conflict' and message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify stale or orphaned agents from prior eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the eval service account, sorted by creation time. Look for agents that are not in an active/in-use state and were created by previous eval runs.

reproductionSteps.label: Delete stale eval agents to free quota headroom
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} for each identified stale eval agent
reproductionSteps.details: After deletion, re-run POST /api/agents to confirm a 201 is now returned and quota is no longer exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-create eval check after cleanup
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) return passing status with vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready].

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — POST /api/agents creation endpoint
affectedAreas.reason: The creation endpoint is the direct point of failure, returning 409 quota exceeded on every invocation by the eval harness.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Swarm quota enforcement layer
affectedAreas.reason: The swarm backend enforces a hard limit of 100 agents per org; this layer is rejecting all new agent creation requests for the eval org.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval harness — agent lifecycle teardown
affectedAreas.reason: The eval harness likely lacks a reliable teardown/cleanup step, allowing agents from prior runs to persist and accumulate against the quota.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — downstream checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)

recommendedNextActions: Immediately audit and delete stale/orphaned swarm agents belonging to the eval service account to restore quota headroom below 100 and unblock the eval.
Add a pre-run teardown step to the eval harness that deletes any agents created by previous eval runs before attempting to create a new one, preventing quota accumulation.
Add a post-run teardown step (with retry logic) to the eval harness to ensure agents are always deleted after each eval cycle, even on failure paths.

Instrument the eval harness to check current agent count against the quota limit before attempting creation, and emit a distinct 'quota_exhausted' eval status rather than a generic 'fail' to make future occurrences immediately diagnosable.
Investigate whether the eval service account should have its own isolated quota allocation or a higher quota limit to prevent interference from other workloads in the same org.

Review whether the swarm backend should return a more specific HTTP status (e.g., 429 Too Many Requests) for quota exhaustion rather than 409 Conflict, to improve signal clarity for monitoring and alerting.
followUpEvals: Add an eval check 'remote-agent-quota-headroom' that calls GET /api/agents, counts active agents, and warns when utilization exceeds 80% of the quota limit (e.g., >80 of 100), firing before exhaustion occurs.
Add an eval check 'remote-agent-teardown' that verifies the agent created during a run is successfully deleted at the end of each eval cycle, catching teardown failures before they accumulate.

Add an eval check that validates the POST /api/agents response is HTTP 201 (not 409) and that the evidence object contains all required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) before proceeding to downstream state/runtime checks.
Add a canary eval that runs on a dedicated isolated eval org with its own quota to decouple eval health from shared org quota consumption.

Add an eval that periodically lists all agents older than 2x the staleAfterMinutes threshold (40 min) owned by the eval service account and flags them as orphaned, enabling proactive cleanup alerting.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Checks Failing with 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No agent can be provisioned, so downstream state polling and runtime readiness checks cannot proceed and produce no required evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally per the eval environment). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T13:48:06–08Z), that cap was already at or above the limit, causing every POST /api/agents call to return 409 with code "conflict" and inner message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three checks, all checks fail at the same point with identical error payloads, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever collected.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' combined with the inner 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' indicates the swarm layer rejected creation because the quota ceiling (100) has been reached, not because of a transient network or auth failure.

All three checks failed within a 2-second window (13:48:06–13:48:08Z) with low latency (914–1250 ms), consistent with an immediate quota-rejection response rather than a timeout or infrastructure fault.
The evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream state or runtime data was collected.
The expectedOutputContract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of which can be populated without a successful agent creation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 live agents from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota and blocking all new agent creation.
[Likely] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown after each run, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is hit.
[Possible] A separate workload or automated process in the same org/environment created agents concurrently, consuming quota before the eval run could proceed.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is misreporting the current agent count as at-limit when it is not.

reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether the org is at or near the 100-agent limit.

reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents with a valid agent creation payload
reproductionSteps.details: Expect HTTP 409 with code 'conflict' and inner message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if quota is exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Look for agents created by previous eval runs that were never deleted. Check creation timestamps and naming conventions used by the eval harness.

reproductionSteps.details: After cleanup, re-trigger the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks to confirm they pass once quota is available.

Add a post-run teardown eval that verifies the agent created during the run was successfully deleted, catching harness cleanup failures before they accumulate.
Add a quota-headroom monitoring check that fires a warning when the org's agent count exceeds 80% of the limit (e.g., >= 80 of 100), providing early warning before evals start failing.

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Swarm Agent Quota Exhausted (HTTP 409 Conflict)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T13:48Z with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no runtime response or chat readiness can be validated.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is rejecting all POST /api/agents requests with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness attempts to create a fresh agent at the start of each run; because the quota ceiling is already met, agent creation fails before any lifecycle, state, or runtime checks can execute. This is a resource-limit exhaustion on the swarm layer, not a service crash or network outage. There is no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals in the supplied data, so impact is scoped to the eval environment's ability to provision test agents.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (endedAt 13:48:06.622Z), remote-agent-state (endedAt 13:48:07.616Z), and remote-agent-runtime (endedAt 13:48:08.530Z).

All three 409 responses carry the identical nested error payload: {"code":"conflict","message":"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100"}, confirming a single shared quota gate is blocking all checks.

Latencies for all three failing calls are well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (914 ms, 994 ms, 1250 ms vs. 20000 ms warning / 60000 ms outage), meaning the swarm rejected requests immediately rather than timing out — consistent with a quota guard returning fast.
The check config marks remote-agent-runtime as required: false, limiting the blast radius to eval coverage rather than a hard service gate.

No evidence of passing sibling checks or alternative endpoints exists in the supplied data, ruling out a partial-route failure and pointing to a quota condition that affects the entire agent-creation path.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Eval or test agents from previous runs were not cleaned up, causing accumulated agent objects to exhaust the 100-agent quota ceiling over time.
[Likely] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/delete step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.

[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval environment and other workloads (e.g., staging, developer sandboxes), and concurrent usage from those workloads has consumed the remaining capacity.
[Less likely] The quota ceiling itself was recently lowered by a configuration change on the swarm backend, causing a previously sufficient limit to become insufficient.
[Unlikely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents and reporting quota exceeded even when slots are available.
